issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may not use an inspection of an unrelated place at an unrelated time to substitute its personal observations for the evidence on record when deciding whether witnesses could identify assailants.
material_facts: The appellate court visited a place unrelated to the alleged offence at a time unrelated to the incident to assess whether people could be identified in darkness.
The appellate court relied on its observations during that visit to reject the identification evidence and acquit the accused, without properly correlating the observations to the evidence on record.
The prosecution appealed the acquittal, which had set aside convictions entered at trial.
issues.conclusion: The inspection was not a permissible local inspection, and the appellate court could not decide the case on its own observations without regard to the evidence on record. The acquittal was set aside and the appeal was remitted for rehearing according to law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 539B of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 permits a judge to inspect the place where the offence allegedly occurred, or another place necessary to view for properly appreciating evidence already given, and requires a memorandum of relevant facts observed. The provision contemplates inspection of the scene’s topography or local peculiarities; it does not authorize an unrelated visit to test identification independently of the record or to substitute personal observations for the evidence. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_acquittal: A prosecution appeal challenges an appellate acquittal that set aside convictions entered at trial.
predicates.inspection_unrelated_to_offence: The appellate court inspected a place and conditions unrelated to the location or time of the alleged offence to test whether witnesses could identify the assailants.
predicates.personal_observations_substituted_for_re: The appellate court relied on its own inspection observations to reject evidence on the record without properly relating those observations to that evidence.
predicates.appellate_judgment_set_aside_and_case_re: The appellate judgment is set aside and the case is sent back for rehearing.

issues.definition: When a prosecution appeal challenges an appellate acquittal and the appellate court has used an unrelated inspection to replace consideration of the evidence on record with its own observations, the judgment is set aside and the case is sent back for rehearing.
